post.description:
Log in with your email (in the `username` field) and password.

This uses the standard OAuth2 password form, which is what makes the
"Authorize" button in Swagger UI work. Send the token you get back as the
header `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on later requests.
After 5 wrong passwords for one email (20 from one IP) in 15 minutes,
login answers 429 Too Many Requests until the window ends.
Invalidate the token you're using right now. Other devices stay logged in.

get.description: Who am I? Handy for checking that your token works.

Liveness: is the process up? Kubernetes restarts the container if this fails.
Deliberately does NOT touch the database: a DB outage should not make
Kubernetes kill every healthy app container in a restart loop.

It also says which build is running: after a deploy, the live smoke test
checks `commit` to prove the NEW version answers, not the old one.

Readiness: can we serve traffic? The load balancer stops sending requests
to this instance while this fails, but nothing gets restarted.

Only the database decides readiness. Redis is reported, but if it's down we
still serve traffic (menus come from PostgreSQL, login protection pauses), so
taking every instance out of the load balancer would turn a small problem
into a full outage.
